text:
Nothing in this session went clearly wrong. The plan step read both rule files first (turns 3-4), then the triage note, hand-off, task and specs, then the code. It wrote the `complex` plan once, at turn 67. I found two small inefficiencies.

- **Repeated reads of the same file:** `main.py` was read at turns 37, 38 and 39, and the pause-findings test at turns 50, 53 and 54. Several other files were read twice (`filing.py`, `child.py`, `cli/improve.py`, `runner.py`). The result sizes differ between reads, so these look like paged reads of large files rather than true re-reads. I can't tell from the view whether each read used an offset, so this is low confidence.
- **Repeated grep:** `improve (backlog|show|aa)\b` was searched at turn 63, then again at turn 65 with `--feedback` added. The second search returned only 73 chars. The change to the pattern added little.

I could not check two points from the view:
- Whether the files opened beyond the hand-off's reading list were justified. That depends on the hand-off's contents, and the plan text is not shown.
- Whether the single `Write` stayed under the 12 KB limit. The plan is `complex` and has no rows, so one write is plausible. The `edit` tool was declared but never used.

The header lists no prompt sections, lessons, skills or subagent types, so the conformance entries below cover the two rule files the prompt names.
